blinding_limits.condition_mapping: No condition mapping was provided or consulted. Only the blinded input packet was read; no original assessor prompts, other files, git history or private reasoning traces were consulted.
blinding_limits.possible_inference: Response wording and differences could allow inference about conditions, so anonymity does not establish perfect blinding. No mapping was inferred or assigned.
blinding_limits.same_model_correlation: This is a same-model AI review; correlated reasoning or errors with submitted AI responses may limit independence. A separate review does not establish independent expert validation.
blinding_limits.constructed_evidence: Facts are synthetic constructed cases, evaluated as supplied rather than verified trial evidence.
blinding_limits.criteria_status: Permissible ranges are frozen investigator criteria, not expert truth. Answer admissibility is judged separately from rationale warrant and calibration; defensible alternatives and ambiguities are retained.
blinding_limits.scope: Signalling-question response review only; no trial, domain, overall, benchmark accuracy or causal claim. Official context was taken from the packet, not externally verified.

facts_used: Unmasked collectors recorded 30-day all-cause death occurrence/date from hospital records and civil registrations.
No causal attribution or severity threshold; identical linkage and follow-up; no supplied differential tracing or misclassification pathway.
limitations_retained: Records may contain errors; complete ascertainment is not established.
Knowledge was unlikely to influence this direct outcome; logical impossibility is not established.
assessments.source_warrant_issue: Minor wording ambiguity: absence of an identified pathway should not be read as logical impossibility. The supplied-procedures limitation keeps the rationale sufficiently bounded.
assessments.reasoning: Box 10 question 4.4 supports a negative answer for nonjudgmental all-cause mortality. No is admissible; probably_no is also defensible because the official wording is likelihood-based. Interpret absence of an identified pathway as bounded to the supplied procedures, not proof of impossibility.

facts_used: Unmasked participants chose their own subjective pain ratings.
Automatic transfer and blinded analysis occurred after ratings were chosen.
limitations_retained: Actual influence and its magnitude are unknown.
assessments.reasoning: Box 10 questions 4.3-4.4 identify participants as assessors and a plausible influence pathway for pain. The response correctly separates possibility from actual or likely influence under 4.5.

facts_used: Only a randomized label is supplied.
No sequence method or credible contextual evidence is supplied.
limitations_retained: Missing reporting does not prove nonrandom allocation.
assessments.reasoning: Box 4 question 1.1 expressly supports no_information when the only method information is a randomized label; section 1.1 does not supply a reasonable probable inference here.

facts_used: Missing 12-week pain data were filled using LOCF, including week-2 ratings.
Treatment-only multiple imputation produced a similar estimate; no plausible-departure sensitivity analysis or assumption validation is supplied.
limitations_retained: Actual missing outcomes and mechanisms remain unknown.
Lack of evidence of protection is not proof of bias.
assessments.reasoning: Box 8 question 3.2 expressly cautions against assuming LOCF or treatment-only imputation corrects missing-data bias. Similar estimates do not supply the missing robustness evidence.

facts_used: Smaller imbalance score deterministically selected treatment; ties always used treatment-code order.
No draw occurred; investigators could calculate the next assignment.
limitations_retained: Conclusion applies to the supplied configuration, not all minimisation procedures.
assessments.reasoning: Explicit deterministic and predictable assignments satisfy the negative rule in Box 4 question 1.1 and override its general minimisation inference. Centralisation is not evidence of randomness.

facts_used: Prespecified independent and opposed arm shifts of missing pain scores covered -2 to +2 points.
Clinicians elicited the range before database lock using relevant external longitudinal data.
The exact selected estimate ranged from -0.74 to -1.26 around -1.00, with confidence intervals on the same side of zero.
limitations_retained: Actual reasons for missingness remain unknown.
Robustness is limited to the elicited range, whose plausibility is supplied rather than independently validated.
No clinical importance threshold is supplied; whether a 0.26-point change counts as little change remains judgmental.
assessments.source_warrant_issue: Plausibility and little-change judgments remain conditional; confidence intervals staying on one side of zero alone do not prove absence of meaningful bias. Here magnitude stability and elicitation support are also cited.
assessments.reasoning: Box 8 question 3.2 permits evidence from plausible-range sensitivity analyses without knowing the actual mechanism. Yes is defensible and within the frozen range; probably_yes is also defensible given judgments about range plausibility and little change. Stable sign alone would be insufficient, but the response also uses magnitude stability and elicitation support.

facts_used: Large multicentre trial run by an experienced trials unit.
Contemporaneous independent audits describe computer-random lists in other trials; journal imposed a 3000-word limit.
limitations_retained: Other-trial audit evidence does not directly document this trial.
No trial-specific algorithm or sequence log is available.
assessments.reasoning: Box 4 question 1.1 and section 1.1 allow a probable inference from credible trial circumstances. The response appropriately avoids a definitive trial-specific method claim.

facts_used: Methods explicitly name minimisation and balancing variables.
A central web service allocated treatments; code, tie handling and logs are unavailable.
limitations_retained: Actual settings and presence of a random element are unconfirmed.
Central web allocation alone does not establish randomness.
assessments.reasoning: Box 4 question 1.1 states minimisation should generally be considered random because it generally includes a random element. Probably_yes applies that source-supported default while preserving uncertainty; yes is also in the frozen permissible range.
